title: Lunch & Learn
intro: A Lunch & Learn is a format: one design question a team keeps debating, every answer to it built for real, and an hour to try them side by side. Nothing here is mocked. Every request really goes to a server and every number is measured while you watch.

origin.text: The format comes from Sam Peterson's Lunch & Learn, the original site of this kind:

topics.title: Is useEffect a Code Smell?
topics.summary: "useEffect is a code smell" overstates a narrower point. Effects are the right tool for syncing with something outside React, and a source of bugs when used as a general "when X changes, do Y". These lessons run each misuse next to its fix, in real React against a real server, and measure the difference.

lessons.title: Start here: the claim and where it comes from
lessons.blurb: What effects are for, where the slogan comes from, and every term the lessons use.

lessons.title: Typing faster than the server
lessons.blurb: Search as you type. An older answer lands last and the page shows results for the wrong query.

lessons.title: Switching users
lessons.blurb: Reset state in an effect and one commit shows the previous user's draft. Every time.

lessons.title: The order placed twice
lessons.blurb: Place an order from an effect, leave, come back, and count the orders on the server.

lessons.title: Fetch, render, fetch again
lessons.blurb: A parent fetches, renders a child, and the child fetches. Time the waterfall.

lessons.title: How rare is the race?
lessons.blurb: Run hundreds of real keystroke pairs on a wired, office or mobile profile and count stale results.

lessons.title: So is it a code smell?
lessons.chip: So is it a code smell?
